report.summary: Cause: in `public/src/store.js`, the failure branch of `load()` set `orders: []`. A failed Refresh therefore emptied the list and left only the error. I removed that line. A failed load now only sets `loading: false` and the error message. The message reads "Could not refresh orders." once a load has succeeded, and "Could not load orders." on a failed first load. The first-load case is unchanged, because the list is empty then anyway. A successful refresh still clears the message. Changing filters still clears the old rows first, so ORD-2 is unaffected. I also added a regression test in `test/store.test.js`. It covers a failed refresh keeping the orders with the refresh message, and the next success clearing the message.
report.verification:
- `npm test`: all 5 tests pass, including the new one.
- I ran the registry check `orders-refresh-keeps-orders` once, against the changed code in a real browser. It sent one HTTP 503 on the orders read, then pressed Refresh. Its two expect steps, `orders-kept` and `refresh-error-shown`, both completed, and the run reported no findings. The screen showed 8 order rows before and after the failed refresh, with an unchanged fingerprint. Later samples show the orders marker hidden (presumably after the final navigation step); I did not look into that.
- I did not record a before-change baseline or run `compare_reports`. The project has no `.recovery-probe/verify.json`, and the tree already held the change when I ran the plan. So I can't quote a before/after verdict. The check covers only one 503 on a refresh of the All list.
- I did not run the other two registry checks, `orders-filter-latest-wins` and `orders-ship-updates-row`, which the plan also selected for `store.js`.
- I stopped the server and browser helper I started, by their process ids.
